hypotheses.confidence_note: Repaired all seven stationary BODY envelopes by rounding every coordinate boundary outward by 0.01 m; this encloses the oriented bodies before residual inflation, including the reported tiny trigonometric overhangs. Actor states, dimensions, adverse modes, residuals, road and safety limits are unchanged. Conditional proposal only, NOT an executable or verified trajectory. Ego initially moves at 5.214907355093433 m/s. The estimated 8.2–8.4 m aisle fits the physical body but cannot contain the required approximately 3.614 m rear-axle disk plus 1 m safety margin and 0.4 m road residual at the initial state. No target change or braking decision can repair that initial conservative road conflict; independent verification must reject execution under these constraints. Parked-body collision constraints may also fail. The finite local scene excludes distant truck, blue sedan, further parked rows, rear bus area and its pedestrians only under explicit no-entry conditions, not claims of absence. Metric geometry and residuals are uncalibrated visual hypotheses.

premises.statement: Model only this finite parking-aisle domain for two seconds, with intended ego travel approximately x=0 to 10 m. Adopt no new unobserved entrant, pedestrian, opening door, or moving vehicle entering this domain. The distant left flatbed, right blue car and further rows remain outside it; traffic and pedestrians behind the rear boundary do not enter. These are falsifiable conditional exclusions, not whole-world absence claims. All seven previously declared nearby parked vehicles are retained. Curbs, planted islands and parking bays are not added to the road polygon.

Assume approximately level local pavement and the stated passenger-vehicle body-size priors. Estimate contact points, body centers and perpendicular parking headings visually using supplied camera axes and perspective. The individually observed left silver MPV is assigned length 4.7 m and width 1.9 m. Its apparent body span, neighboring parked noses and converging curb edges support an approximate 8.2–8.4 m aisle. Front and rear images support a continuous patch from x=-6 to 18 m; the far bend is outside the intended route. Intrinsics/extrinsics establish axes, not certified depth. Residuals represent uncalibrated remaining position/shape error. Stationary source rectangles round each exact nominal body extent outward by 0.01 m solely for robust geometric enclosure; this padding is not residual uncertainty.

All declared vehicles appear parked in bays. Adopt bodies stationary at their stated reference centers and orientations, retaining an adverse mode with absolute ground speed at most 0.1 m/s in any direction and yaw deviation at most 0.03 rad from the stated orientation throughout this interval. Each adverse rectangle contains the complete rotated body and up to 0.2 m reference-to-future translation, including t=0. Its 0.3 m coordinate padding covers translation and rotation spread, separately from residual uncertainty. These two retained modes exhaust the explicitly adopted local movement conditions. Faster pull-outs and opening doors are excluded, not ruled out by observation.

Estimate side-camera evidence centers directly in fixed reference axes incorporating supplied ego poses and camera orientations. Mercedes evidence age is 0.042121 s and Nissan age is 0.007616 s. Under the retained actor-speed bound of 0.1 m/s, evidence-to-reference displacement is at most 0.004213 m and 0.000762 m respectively, covering both declared scenarios. Native reference centers use stationary estimates; each 0.5 m alignment residual includes this displacement and visual transformation error. Actor-motion bounds are additional assumptions, not inferred from ego compensation.

This supports the finite road and actor hypotheses but does not justify widening the road to fit the conservative disk.
